nameOrigin.text: The town takes its name from Crested Butte Mountain, which rises to the northeast.

founded.text: Howard F. Smith established the settlement at the junction of Coal Creek and the Slate River; it was known as Crested Butte by the summer of 1878.

timeline.text: Settlers looking for precious metals were in the area as early as 1874.
Crested Butte, a supply center for nearby mining camps, was incorporated.
Coal mines and coke ovens made the Crested Butte area the state's leading mountain coal operation by 1882.
The major coal mines shut down.
The Crested Butte Historic District was listed on the National Register on May 29, 1974.

trails.name: Crested Butte Nordic trails
trails.size: 55 km of groomed trails for skiing and snowshoeing
trails.trailhead: The Nordic Center, 620 2nd Street (Mountain Express stop: 2nd and Whiterock); more trailheads on Peanut Lake Road and at Town Ranch behind the school on 9th Street
trails.season: The Nordic season, November to April; the trails stay closed to all uses until grooming starts.
trails.dogs: Only on the dog-friendly trails, and every dog needs a trail pass; no more than two dogs per skier.
trails.fee: A trail pass: $30 a day for adults 19 to 64, $20 for 65 to 69, free from 70, $10 for 18 and under; $10 a day for a dog. Day passes are sold at the Nordic Center.

trails.name: Town Ranch
trails.length: 3 km, groomed for skiing, snowshoeing, walking and fat biking
trails.trailhead: Town Ranch, behind the school on 9th Street
trails.season: Groomed in the Nordic season; the trails stay closed to all uses until grooming starts.
